lead: The spark must arrive at a crank angle, not an instant, so the engine control unit works in degrees. It charges the coil for a fixed dwell time, fires the plug a set number of degrees before top dead centre, and retards that angle when the knock sensor complains. Spark advance decides torque, fuel economy, emissions and piston survival. Every petrol car on Indian roads runs this loop thousands of times a minute, at little extra cost once the ECU exists for fuelling.
prereq: You need: 4.4 for maps and closed loop, 4.5 for load and shared corrections, and Unit 2 for how the coil and plug work.

blocks.text: The coil stores energy only while its primary circuit is closed. Current rises towards a limit set by winding resistance, typically 4 A to 6 A. Stored energy is ½LI², where L is primary inductance in henry and I is current in ampere. Opening the circuit collapses the field; the secondary makes high voltage and the plug arcs.

Dwell time t<sub>d</sub> is how long, in milliseconds, the ECU holds the primary closed before the break. It is fixed for a coil and battery voltage. A low battery makes current rise more slowly, so the ECU lengthens dwell.
Dwell angle θ<sub>d</sub> is the same interval in crank degrees. The ECU works in degrees because the spark must land at a crank angle.

blocks.where: θ<sub>d</sub> is dwell angle in crank degrees; t<sub>d</sub> is dwell time in milliseconds; N is engine speed in rpm; 360 is degrees in one revolution and 60 000 is milliseconds in one minute.

blocks.text: At 3000 rpm one millisecond is 18 crank degrees, so 3.0 ms spans 54 degrees. At 6000 rpm one millisecond is 36 degrees; the ECU shortens dwell to 2.0 ms. The window must fit between sparks.

sections.h3: Spark advance, MBT and the knock limit

blocks.text: The mixture needs time to burn. The flame starts at the plug, crosses the chamber, and for best torque the pressure peak should fall about 10 to 15 degrees after top dead centre. So the plug fires before TDC. Spark advance θ<sub>adv</sub> is the crank angle in degrees before top dead centre (BTDC) at which the plug fires.

More advance starts the burn earlier and pulls the pressure peak towards TDC, so torque rises; past a point the gain stops. Minimum advance for best torque (MBT) is the smallest advance giving maximum torque. Beyond MBT, extra advance adds heat and knock and buys nothing.

Knock is unburnt end gas ahead of the flame front igniting by itself, giving a sharp pressure spike that can crack a piston. The knock limit is the most advance the engine survives at that speed and load. It drops with low-octane petrol, hot intake air, hot coolant and carbon deposits.

The ECU fires at θ<sub>spark</sub> = min(θ<sub>MBT</sub>, θ<sub>knock</sub> − Δ), where θ<sub>spark</sub> is firing advance, θ<sub>MBT</sub> is MBT advance, θ<sub>knock</sub> is knock-limit advance, all in degrees BTDC, and Δ is a 1 to 3 degree safety margin. At low speed and high load the knock limit usually sits below MBT, so the engine runs retarded (less advance) and gives up torque.

sections.h3: The spark map and its corrections

blocks.text: Base advance comes from a two-dimensional map, with engine speed on one axis and load on the other. Load is air trapped per cycle, measured by the mass air flow sensor or computed from manifold pressure as in 4.5. This is the map lookup of 4.4 applied to one output.

items: Light load, 1500 to 2500 rpm: 30 to 45 degrees BTDC. Charge dilute, burn slow, knock unlikely.
Wide open throttle: 10 to 20 degrees BTDC. Dense charge burns fast and knocks easily.
Idle: 5 to 15 degrees BTDC, nudged every firing to hold idle speed.

Corrections are summed and clamped to a safe band for that speed and load. The same sensor corrections appear in fuel control, where they change injector open time instead of coil timing.

sections.h3: Closed-loop knock control and misfire detection

blocks.text: The knock sensor is a piezo accelerometer bolted to the block (Unit 3). It rings at 5 to 15 kHz when the block rings from knock. The ECU band-pass filters around the knock frequency, rectifies, and compares the peak with a speed-dependent threshold.

items: Knock seen: retard by 2 to 4 degrees, for that cylinder if coils are per cylinder.
No knock: advance slowly, about 0.5 to 1 degree per firing.
Knock returns: retard again. Timing settles just under the knock limit and hunts.
Knock persists at full retard: enrich the mixture, reduce boost, or both.

blocks.text: Fast retard and slow advance keep the loop stable. Retard is immediate because knock damages metal in seconds; advance is slow because a few degrees too far is heard after the next firing.

Misfire shows up as a crank that does not speed up. The crank sensor gives a pulse every few degrees, and the ECU times each segment to get angular acceleration. A firing cylinder accelerates the crank; a dead one does not. Comparing each cylinder with the average gives a misfire index, which sets the on-board diagnostic (OBD-II) code (Unit 6) and protects the catalytic converter from raw fuel.

figure.caption: Time runs in crank degrees from the moment the coil starts charging. The spark at 54 degrees is 25 degrees before top dead centre; the burn finishes about 31 degrees after it.

spec.aria: Running in crank degrees from the moment the coil starts charging: the primary stays closed for 54 degrees, the spark fires at 54 degrees and lasts about 18 degrees, and the burn carries on to 110 degrees.

examples.question: At 3000 rpm the ECU wants the spark 25 degrees before top dead centre and a dwell of 3.0 ms. (a) How many crank degrees is 3.0 ms at this speed? (b) At what crank angle before TDC must the coil start charging? (c) At 6000 rpm the coil needs only 2.0 ms: find the new dwell angle and the new start angle.
steps: (b) Charging starts 54 degrees before the spark, and the spark is 25 degrees BTDC: 25 + 54 = 79 degrees BTDC.
(c) Dwell angle = 2.0 × 36 = 72 degrees; charging starts at 25 + 72 = 97 degrees BTDC.
examples.answer: The 3.0 ms dwell is 54 degrees and charging starts 79 degrees BTDC; at 6000 rpm the 2.0 ms dwell is 72 degrees and charging starts 97 degrees BTDC.
examples.check:
rpm1 = 3000
deg_per_ms1 = rpm1 * 360 / 60 / 1000
print(deg_per_ms1)
dwell1 = 3.0 * deg_per_ms1
print(dwell1)
print(25 + dwell1)
rpm2 = 6000
deg_per_ms2 = rpm2 * 360 / 60 / 1000
print(deg_per_ms2)
dwell2 = 2.0 * deg_per_ms2
print(dwell2)
print(25 + dwell2)

traps: Adding milliseconds to degrees. Convert first: degrees = ms × N × 0.006.
Treating dwell angle as constant. Dwell time is set by the coil; angle grows with speed.
Calling advance a time. 25 degrees BTDC is about 1.4 ms at 3000 rpm.
Saying the ECU always runs at MBT. It runs at min(MBT, knock limit − margin).
Mixing loops: knock control retards spark; misfire detection only reports.

quiz.q: Define dwell time and dwell angle, with units.
quiz.a: Dwell time is the interval the coil primary stays closed before the break, in milliseconds. Dwell angle is the same interval in crank degrees.

quiz.q: Why does the ECU fire the plug before top dead centre?
quiz.a: The burn takes time. Firing early places the pressure peak about 10 to 15 degrees after TDC, where it pushes the piston hardest.

quiz.q: Why does the knock limit usually sit below MBT at low speed and high load?
quiz.a: A dense charge at low speed has a long time to absorb heat, so the end gas auto-ignites at an advance lower than the one that would give best torque.

quiz.q: At 2400 rpm the ECU sets a 2.5 ms dwell and 20 degrees BTDC. Find the dwell angle and the angle at which charging starts.
quiz.a: 2400 rpm = 40 rev/s = 40 × 360 = 14 400 degrees/s = 14.4 degrees/ms. Dwell angle = 2.5 × 14.4 = 36 degrees. Charging starts at 20 + 36 = 56 degrees BTDC.

quiz.q: A car knocks on 91-octane petrol but not on 95-octane. What does the ECU do differently, and what happens to fuel economy?
quiz.a: On 91 the knock limit is lower, so the loop retards further below MBT, torque falls, the driver opens the throttle more and fuel consumption rises. On 95 the knock limit clears MBT, the ECU runs at MBT and gets best torque for the least fuel.

quiz.q: How does the ECU detect misfire, and which sensor does it use?
quiz.a: It times each crank segment from the crank position sensor and computes angular acceleration. A firing cylinder speeds the crank up; a misfiring one does not. Comparing each cylinder with the average gives a misfire index.

beyond: Not for the exam. Production engines now do per-cylinder knock detection, using a sensor per bank or ion current across the plug gap, so retard applies to one cylinder. Model-based spark control predicts knock from cylinder-pressure history instead of waiting to hear it. On downsized turbo petrol engines, spark retard after a cold start pushes hot exhaust into the catalyst. Search for ion current sensing, cylinder-pressure-based combustion control, and knock window next.
